description.value: The study reassessed an existing sample to examine whether lifetime DSM-assessed cocaine withdrawal status modulates neural reactivity biases to drug- versus food-related reward cues, and whether drug-use history and psychopathic traits further influence these biases.

spans.text: The current study offers insight into these conflicting positions by using secondary analyses to assess how a history of DSM-assessed withdrawal influences the magnitude of bias in neural reactivity to drug- and/or food-related reward cues.

design.value: Secondary analysis of a cue-reactivity fMRI study comparing cocaine-dependent participants with and without lifetime withdrawal to non-dependent controls using a mixed-model flexible-factorial Group × VideoType design, followed by hierarchical regression analyses among dependent participants.
